_readme: Every extension and code system open-twin invents must be declared here.
The HL7 validator treats an unresolvable EXTENSION as an error, not a warning —
unlike an unresolvable CodeSystem, which is only a warning. So an extension that
nobody has declared fails the build, and the validator itself is the gate: there
is no separate script to keep in sync.
This is the beginning of the implementation guide. Publishing it properly (with
SUSHI and the IG Publisher) is tracked as connector-completion work; these
generated definitions exist so that CI can validate today rather than after the
Adding an entry is a deliberate act. If a connector wants a new extension, it
declares it here with what it means and what it attaches to.

codeSystems.title: Oura vendor concepts
codeSystems.description: Measures reported by the Oura Ring v2 API that have no verified LOINC or SNOMED CT concept.

codeSystems.title: Google Health vendor concepts
codeSystems.description: Measures reported by the Google Health API v4 that have no verified LOINC or SNOMED CT concept.

codeSystems.title: VITRONIC BodyLoop vendor concepts
codeSystems.description: Body-scan measurement paths reported by the VITRONIC BodyLoop scanner. No standard terminology covers 3D anthropometry.

codeSystems.title: open-twin connector identity
codeSystems.description: Identifies which connector produced a bundle, and at which version, so output generated before a correction can be told apart from output generated after it.

extensions.title: Oura reported age
extensions.description: Age in years as reported by Oura. Oura supplies no date of birth; a birthDate was previously derived from this and is not, which is why the age is carried as-is.

extensions.title: Oura sleep day
extensions.description: The calendar day Oura assigns a sleep period to, which is not necessarily the day the period started.

extensions.title: Oura heart rate source
extensions.description: Which Oura context produced a heart-rate sample, e.g. awake, rest, sleep, workout.

extensions.title: Oura heart rate unix timestamp
extensions.description: Oura's own unix timestamp for the sample, in milliseconds. Retained verbatim because it is documented in milliseconds while a sibling field is in seconds, and conflating them is a 1000x error.

extensions.title: Oura workout day
extensions.description: The calendar day Oura assigns a workout to.

extensions.title: Oura workout label
extensions.description: The user's free-text label for a workout.

extensions.title: Oura workout intensity
extensions.description: Oura's intensity classification: easy, moderate or hard.

extensions.title: Oura workout source
extensions.description: How the workout was recorded: manual, autodetected, confirmed or workout_heart_rate.

extensions.title: Oura ring configuration id
extensions.description: Identifier of the ring configuration record a resource was derived from. Allowed on Observation as well as Device because sleep Observations carry the ring that produced them: declaring it Device-only surfaced that mismatch, which is the point of declaring it at all. Observation.device is the primary link; this extension survives for the case where no Device resource was built.

extensions.title: Oura ring colour
extensions.description: Cosmetic finish of the ring, as reported by Oura.

extensions.title: Oura ring design
extensions.description: Design variant of the ring, as reported by Oura.

extensions.title: VITRONIC measurement hidden
extensions.description: True when the scanner operator suppressed this measurement. Carried rather than dropped because a suppressed measurement published as status 'final' with no indication is worse than one a receiver can filter. Whether it should instead downgrade Observation.status needs clinical review.

extensions.title: VITRONIC marker type
extensions.description: The scanner's classification of an anatomical landmark.

extensions.title: VITRONIC skeleton series path
extensions.description: Path identifying the skeleton series a cross-section was taken from, so a measurement can be traced back to its landmarks.

extensions.title: Google Health data source
extensions.description: Provenance of a data point: which application, platform and recording method produced it. This is what lets a consumer decide whether an Oura heart rate and a Google Health heart rate are comparable, which is the reason this project exists.

subExtensions.title: Source application
subExtensions.description: The application that wrote the data point.

subExtensions.title: Source platform
subExtensions.description: The platform the data point originated on, e.g. FITBIT.

subExtensions.title: Recording method
subExtensions.description: How the value was recorded: measured, manually entered, or automatically recorded.
